content.text:
Let me analyze this ticket.

The employee Richard Davis (E011) requests write access to Payroll.

There are two conflicting notes:

Note 1 (from HR presumably): full_time, Payroll Specialist, recommend write.
Note 2 (from Security): contractor, basic security training, recommend read.

The two notes conflict on employment type. As Approver, I need to make a decision based on the information available. The Security note says the Security DB shows contractor with basic training, differing from the earlier note claiming full-time. The Security DB is probably authoritative for employment type/security training. The recommendation for contractors with basic training is read (write requires advanced training).

So the max access for contractor with basic training is read. Requested write exceeds max, so grant max = read.

Also, even if we considered full-time Payroll Specialist, write would be allowed (system owned by role, full-time up to write, admin only if role owns... actually full-time can have up to write, admin only if role owns system. Payroll Specialist owns Payroll? The note says Payroll is owned by the Payroll Specialist role, write is within policy). But the security note indicates contractor status. Given conflicting info, the security DB note says contractor. Hmm.

As the Approver, I should decide. The safest and per policy based on the security DB: contractor with basic training → max read. Grant read.

Let me submit decision: read.
